Proposed DSAMS platform service fee

The approved product requirement for this edition is KSh 20 per registered parent / guardian account, per school term. Each parent account renews its access payment every term while registered and using DSAMS. The charge is per parent account, not per learner, and is separate from school fees and other school charges.

The charging interval is termly: KSh 20 per parent account for each term. Before live collection, publish the term dates, payment due date, grace period, access status after non-payment, exemptions, refunds and dispute process. Obtain appropriate legal, tax, child-data and payment-provider review. This demo does not collect money.

Payment controls

  • Use a vetted payment provider; never store card PINs, mobile-money PINs or raw credentials.
  • Unique transaction references and idempotency prevent duplicate posting.
  • Webhook signature verification and reconciliation before marking invoices paid.
  • Separate school funds and platform revenue in accounting and reporting.
  • Receipts, refunds, reversals, approvals and immutable audit records.

National Scale & Capacity Architecture

A scale-out production blueprint for a national network of schools, learners, parents, teachers and institutions.

Edition 4.3.7 · Architecture plan
Important distinction: This edition removes any proposed fixed user ceiling from the product design, but no software can promise unlimited or error-free capacity. Supporting millions—or designing toward a billion registered accounts—depends on the cloud infrastructure, database design, network capacity, security controls, operating budget and repeated load testing. This browser demo itself has not been load-tested and cannot serve millions of simultaneous users.
🌐

Elastic application services

Stateless application/API services behind global traffic management and load balancers, with horizontal autoscaling as demand rises and safe scale-in when demand falls.

🗄️

Distributed data layer

Partitioned and, where justified, sharded databases; indexed access patterns; read replicas; connection pooling; tenant-aware access controls and tested failover.

⚡

Fast content delivery

CDN delivery for static assets, carefully scoped caching, regional edge delivery and compression to reduce repeated work on core services.

📨

Queues for busy periods

Background queues for bulk result uploads, notifications, analytics, document processing and reports, with retries, deduplication, dead-letter handling and visible job status.

🛡️

Security at national scale

API gateway, web application firewall, DDoS protection, rate limits, bot controls, encryption, least privilege, MFA and strict school-tenant isolation.

🧭

Monitoring & recovery

Central metrics, logs, traces, alerting, capacity forecasting, multi-zone resilience, independent encrypted backups and rehearsed disaster recovery.

How DSAMS handles growth

Growth stageProduction approachRequired proof before expansion
Initial pilotOne production region across multiple availability zones; managed database; tenant isolation; monitoring and backups.Security review, recovery drill, functional and baseline load tests.
National adoptionAutoscaling services, CDN, queue workers, read replicas, partitioned data and automated capacity alerts.Peak-season load tests, queue-drain tests, failover exercise and cost forecast.
Very large / global-scale ambitionSharding or distributed data services where measured bottlenecks justify them; multi-region strategy; regional routing and tested data replication.Independent architecture review, multi-region disaster test, privacy/legal review and sustained stress tests.

Capacity and reliability rules

  • No arbitrary product-level account cap: the production design should not hard-code a small maximum number of schools or users. Actual capacity must be expanded by provisioning and testing infrastructure.
  • Registered users are not concurrent users: one billion accounts in a directory is a different engineering problem from millions of people active at the same second. DSAMS must model both peak concurrency and peak requests per second.
  • Protect each school: every request must be authenticated and scoped to the correct school/tenant; one school's load or permissions must not expose another school's records.
  • Keep heavy work off the request path: large uploads, bulk analytics, AI tasks and mass notifications should run asynchronously and report progress.
  • Graceful degradation: during exceptional demand, preserve sign-in, essential learner records and safe data writes first; defer non-critical reports and bulk notifications rather than letting the whole platform fail.
  • AI is an operator, not a capacity substitute: Generali Autopilot may monitor approved health signals and trigger pre-approved scaling/runbooks after owner authorisation. It cannot create cloud capacity by itself or bypass security, budgets, privacy or change controls.
  • Cost and abuse controls: budgets, quotas, anomaly detection, rate limits and human escalation are required to prevent runaway cloud bills or malicious traffic.
  • Data protection: student and parent data require lawful purpose, minimum collection, retention controls, access logging and independent security/privacy review before live rollout.

Go-live acceptance gates

Before claiming any user capacity, the production team must publish measured results for concurrent sessions, requests per second, upload throughput, analytics queue processing, error rate, latency, recovery time and recovery point. Tests must include peak examination/result-release periods, traffic spikes, database failover and a regional outage simulation.

Current status: These are architecture requirements and a roadmap displayed in the demo. No production cloud cluster, distributed database, autoscaling policy, billion-user capacity, live monitoring or government integration is created by this HTML update. Capacity claims must wait for independently reviewed tests on the deployed system.

5. Security and governance control checklist

These are mandatory design requirements before handling real school or learner information.

  • Separate tenant data so one school cannot view another school's private records.
  • Use secure sign-in, multi-factor authentication for privileged users, and role-based permissions.
  • Encrypt data in transit and at rest; protect backups and manage keys securely.
  • Keep tamper-evident audit logs for access, mark changes, result approvals, billing and administrator actions.
  • Require teacher submission and authorised school approval before academic results are released.
  • Apply Kenyan data-protection requirements, child-data safeguards, retention rules and access/deletion processes.
  • Use server-side subscription checks; never rely on browser-only online locks or local storage for payment status.
  • Perform security testing, recovery testing and independent review before launch.

08 · Production engineering requirements

What must be built before real launch

  • Central PostgreSQL database with strict school tenant isolation and row-level security.
  • Production Generali administrator identity, MFA, recovery and immutable audit logging.
  • Separate verified beneficiary profiles and ledger accounts for Generali and every school.
  • Payment-provider split routing or separate merchant accounts, signed webhooks, reconciliation, refunds and chargeback handling.
  • Parent/teacher authentication, school-scoped permissions and guardian verification.
  • Live academic synchronization with validation, version history and school-level access control.
  • Notification gateway, delivery receipts, consent/preferences and message-rate controls.
  • AI service identity with least privilege, action allowlist, approval tokens, monitoring and emergency shutdown.

DSAMS Access & Subscription Policy

Proposed individual access charge and separate institutional arrangements.

Proposed individual subscription: KES 20 per user, per school term, for eligible individual DSAMS accounts such as parents, students and teachers. Kenya has three school terms in a typical academic year, so the proposed total would be KES 60 per year if the fee is approved and all three terms are billed. This is a proposal only; no payment is collected in this demonstration.

Individual users

  • Parent / guardian account: proposed KES 20 per term.
  • Student account: proposed KES 20 per term.
  • Teacher account: proposed KES 20 per term.
  • Any other individual account: only after a published fee schedule and clear consent.

Institutions

Schools, colleges and other institutions will have a separate institutional subscription or service agreement. Their pricing, billing cycle, exemptions and account limits are deliberately left configurable for a later decision by Generali.

Strict separation: The proposed DSAMS subscription is not a TSC recruitment, registration, promotion or transfer fee. TSC recruitment is free through official TSC channels. DSAMS must not charge users to apply for a TSC job, and no payment guarantees employment, transfer, admission or approval. Before real collection, publish terms, refund rules, receipts, data-protection notices and a compliant payment integration. No payment gateway is connected here.

6. AI notifications, monitoring and national-scale readiness

With General's approval, the existing Generali AI Autopilot can monitor authorised DSAMS workflows, flag missing assessment submissions, prepare reminders, track portal notices entered through approved channels and create operational reports. Schools, parents, teachers and learners retain their own optional AI controls.

  • Notifications should be queued, deduplicated, rate-limited and retried safely; sensitive learner notices must go only to verified, authorised recipients.
  • Government portal alerts are not automatically received by DSAMS today. Production requires official notification feeds, API access or a permitted integration agreement.
  • Autopilot must not invent official results, submit unapproved scores, bypass KNEC logins, change learner records without an audit trail or override school data boundaries.
10-million-user capacity: This HTML demonstration does not support ten million concurrent users. Production capacity requires a cloud-native backend, horizontally scaled application services, CDN/static delivery, queue-based background processing, caching, database partitioning and tenant isolation, observability, disaster recovery, security reviews and independently run load/stress tests. Capacity must be proven against agreed peak concurrency and response-time targets before a national launch.

AI Authority, System Permissions & Automatic Backup

Governed by General Fabrigas — CEO & Project Manager. AI access is permission-based, logged, limited to approved tasks and revocable.

Important security boundary: General's approval can authorise defined DSAMS functions, but it must not bypass user privacy, school data separation, safeguarding, legal obligations, or security controls. The AI cannot grant itself permissions, erase audit records, or approve its own actions.

GENERALI AI MONITORING DEPARTMENT — MASTER AUTOPILOT

Owner-controlled operations mode. This switch is for Generali's internal administration only. It does not force AI use on schools, parents, teachers or students.

Authority boundary: When enabled, the AI operations assistant is authorised to coordinate and monitor the Generali workflows covered by General's saved permissions, run routine permitted tasks, monitor system health, prepare reports and manage approved backup jobs. It is not an unrestricted superuser: it cannot bypass school data separation, privacy safeguards, safeguarding rules, security controls, or legal duties. High-impact actions such as payments/refunds, deleting records, suspending accounts, changing privileged access, releasing sensitive learner records, or changing the AI's own permissions require separate authorised approval.

AUTOPILOT OFF — awaiting explicit owner approval and saved AI permissions.

What autopilot coordinates: approved Generali administration queues, routine workflow follow-ups, system-health monitoring, analytics/report preparation, backup monitoring and recovery readiness. All actions must be logged.

2. Automatic backup and recovery

Backup policy: scheduled encrypted server-side backups, version history, off-site copy, integrity checks, restore testing and a protected audit log are required for the live platform. Backup access should be available to the authorised system owner and designated recovery administrators; AI may monitor and initiate approved backup jobs but must not be able to silently delete or overwrite recovery copies.

Automatic backup is not enabled. No backup has been created yet.

Demo limitation: automatic checkpoints are stored only in this browser's local storage on this device. They are not a secure off-site backup, may be lost if browser data is cleared, and do not protect against device loss. The HTML download preserves this app version; the JSON export preserves selected demo records. Production backups require a secure backend, database snapshots, encrypted object storage in a separate account/region, retention rules and tested restoration.

3. Mandatory production safeguards

  • Least-privilege permissions, scoped by role and school tenant.
  • Multi-factor authentication for General and privileged administrators.
  • Separate approval for payments, account deletion, access changes and bulk export.
  • Immutable audit trail recording who approved what, when, and why.
  • Encryption in transit and at rest; secrets kept on the server, never in browser code.
  • Daily database backups plus point-in-time recovery where supported; independent off-site copies.
  • Regular restore drills and documented recovery objectives.
  • AI never accesses private learner records unless the specific task, lawful basis and permissions allow it.

Registered School Secure Access

A school must be approved by Generali, activated, and use its own unique DSAMS code before its school workspace can open.

School sign-in demonstration

Access is checked against approved and activated school records in this browser demo.

Security rules

  • Pending, rejected or unactivated schools are denied.
  • Each school code is unique and tied to one school tenant.
  • Every staff member, teacher and parent must have an individual account.
  • Production sign-in must add secure password hashing, MFA, session expiry and server-side role checks.
  • A school code identifies the tenant; it is not a password and must never be the only authentication factor.

DSAMS Online Teaching & Learning

A school-controlled learning area for live lessons, recorded lessons, assignments, revision and learner support while students are away from school.

Schedule a live lesson

This prototype schedules a lesson and stores a meeting link; it does not itself provide video streaming. Production can integrate an approved video-conferencing/streaming provider.

Learning safeguards

  • Teachers create lessons only within their assigned school and classes.
  • Parents/guardians receive school-authorised notices and lesson schedules.
  • Use waiting rooms, teacher controls, attendance logs and reporting tools.
  • Do not expose learner contact details or meeting links publicly.
  • Record lessons only with school approval, appropriate notices and lawful consent.
  • Provide accessible notes and low-bandwidth alternatives.
